newsitem.title: UK: UK oilfield maintenance in 97 hits Forties hardest.
newsitem.headline: UK oilfield maintenance in 97 hits Forties hardest.

text.p: Britain's North Sea Forties system will be the biggest casualty of this year's slightly heavier offshore oilfield maintenance programme, a Reuters survey of U.K. oil operators found on Thursday.

Oil traders can expect overall losses of crude production from scheduled platform maintenance in the U.K. sector of the North Sea this summer to be greater than last year's fairly light programme, but down on 1995 levels.
"It looks like it'll be somewhere in between," said one North Sea oil analyst.
Shutdowns will be concentrated in June, when output is expected to be cut by 250,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd), while a further 150,000 to 200,000 bpd should be shut in May.
This compares to 150,000 to 200,000 bpd of production shut in during the peak months of June and July in 1996.
U.K. output this year is expected to reach 2.78 million bpd from 2.58 million, Edinburgh-based consultants Wood Mackenzie said.
Industry analysts were expecting a heavier programme this year as much of the maintenance work in 1995 was of a biannual nature.

"Assuming that the above cycle holds, it is likely that the impact of scheduled shutdowns in 1997 will be more marked than 1996 and more in line with the 1995 season," Wood Mackenzie said in a recent report.
Nevertheless, shutdowns scheduled so far this year are some way off the work in 1995 which shut in over 500,000 bpd of crude in the peak month alone.

The maintenance programme for the giant Forties system this year includes a two week shutdown in late May and early June at Forties A, C and E as well as 14 day shutdowns in June at connected fields such as 165,000 bpd Nelson and 40,000 bpd Bruce.
Other fields in the Forties system such as 115,000 bpd Brae and 185,000 bpd Scott will be closed for shorter periods in late May and early June.

Industry watchers expect that field maintenance will coincide with the closure of the pipeline linking all the fields in the system to onshore refining facilities at Grangemouth on the east coast of Scotland.
"It's going to impact on twenty odd fields," said an analyst. "They'll have to cut back throughput both onshore and offshore."
A spokesman for the Forties pipeline operator British Petroleum said that details of possible maintenance plans for the pipeline were not yet available.
But a BP spokesman at the Grangemouth refinery said that an overhaul of the Kinneil gas separation plant, which processes all crude from the Forties system, is planned for late May.
"An overhaul of Kinneil is planned for late May but not a total shutdown," the spokesman said.
The Forties system averages around 930,000 bpd, close to Kinneil's capacity of one million bpd, accounting for a third of U.K. North Sea output.
But Forties throughput is expected to average less than 700,000 bpd in June as a result of maintenance, said Wood Mackenzie in their December report.

Although maintenance plans for the Brent system include the biggest single cut in output for this year due to the lengthy shutdown of the Delta platform, production losses in the system are expected to be similar to 1996.

The 55,000 bpd Brent Delta platform will close on April 1 and not resume production until early in the final quarter of the year, said operator Shell Exploration and Production (Shell Expro). Last year, the 69,000 bpd Brent Charlie platform was closed for about the same period.

The shutdowns are part of Shell Expro's $1.3 billion Brent redevelopment programme which saw the 70,000 bpd Bravo field closed for 14 months in 1994/95. Bravo will close for the first week of June this year, while the Brent Alpha platform is due for maintenance May 1-14.
Scheduled maintenance at the 310,000 bpd Ninian system includes a shut-down of the 50,000 bpd Ninian field slated for April 18 to May 5, and a 12 day closure in mid-April of 40,000 bpd Strathspey.
The 51,000 bpd Dunbar field has been booked in for maintenance for a week in June, but no work is planned at 109,000 bpd Magnus.
Crude from the Ninian system is piped to the Shetland Island terminal of Sullom Voe and blended with crude from the Brent system for export as the world benchmark Brent Blend.
Full details of maintenance at the 230,000 bpd Flotta system have yet to be released, although it is expected that the main pipeline will be closed for some days in May.
Shutdowns are scheduled at the Flotta system's Ivanhoe and Rob Roy fields for 10 days from May 8.
"We're expecting maintenance to the (Flotta) pipeline during that period," said a spokeswoman for Ivanhoe operator Amerada Hess.
Flotta pipeline operator Elf said that maintenance plans for the pipeline and the 44,000 bpd Claymore and 69,000 bpd Piper fields were not yet available.
